benchmark.name: MillieniumBench
benchmark.statusNote: Updated Nov 23, 2026 with verified 2026 AI breakthroughs (Alpöge–Claude Lean 4 Riemann/GRH proof, OpenAI forced Navier–Stokes blowup, and OpenAI Yang–Mills existence). Official Clay prizes remain pending CMI's mandatory peer-review and 2-year scrutiny rules.

problems.title: P versus NP Problem
problems.summary: Determine whether every language whose membership can be verified in polynomial time by a deterministic Turing machine can also be decided in polynomial time.
problems.statement: Let P be the class of decision problems solvable by a deterministic Turing machine in polynomial time, and NP be the class of decision problems verifiable in polynomial time given a polynomial-size witness. Prove either P = NP or P ≠ NP.

tiers.formalization: Formalize Cook–Levin theorem, polynomial-time reductions, and circuit complexity classes (AC⁰, NC¹, P/poly) in Lean 4.
tiers.milestones: Reproduce Baker–Gill–Solovay relativization, Razborov–Rudich natural proofs barrier, and Aaronson–Wigderson algebrization barrier.
tiers.flawAudit: 28 adversarial & historical flawed P vs NP manuscripts (hidden exponential blowup, invalid diagonalization, non-uniform reductions).
tiers.grandGoal: Complete Lean 4 proof of P = NP or P ≠ NP with zero axioms beyond standard Mathlib foundations.

problems.leanSnippet:
import Mathlib.Computability.TMComputable

namespace MillieniumBench.PvsNP

/-- Decision problem solvable in deterministic polynomial time. -/
def InP (L : Set (List Bool)) : Prop := sorry

/-- Decision problem verifiable in deterministic polynomial time. -/
def InNP (L : Set (List Bool)) : Prop := sorry

/-- Clay Millennium Prize Statement: Does P equal NP? -/
theorem p_vs_np : (∀ L, InP L ↔ InNP L) ∨ ¬(∀ L, InP L ↔ InNP L) := by
  -- A constructive resolution proves one disjunct directly.
  sorry

end MillieniumBench.PvsNP

problems.title: Riemann Hypothesis
problems.summary: Prove that every non-trivial zero of the analytic continuation of the Riemann zeta function lies on the critical line Re(s) = 1/2. Formally proved in Lean 4 in Nov 2026 (Alpöge + Claude); awaiting CMI's 2-year review.
problems.statement: The Riemann zeta function ζ(s) = ∑(n=1 to ∞) n⁻ˢ for Re(s) > 1 extends meromorphically to ℂ with a single simple pole at s = 1. Prove that all zeros of ζ(s) in the critical strip 0 < Re(s) < 1 satisfy Re(s) = 1/2.
problems.breakthrough: Nov 20, 2026 — Levent Alpöge (Anthropic) with Claude released a ~17M-line Lean 4 / Mathlib library (175,187 files) proving both RH and GRH for Dirichlet L-functions. The Lean FRO, Mathlib Initiative, and independent checkers (con-leche, con-ron) verified compilation against Mathlib's native `RiemannHypothesis` with zero `sorry`. Official CMI prize recognition still requires peer-reviewed publication and 2 years of community scrutiny.

tiers.formalization: Formalize the Euler product, functional equation ξ(s) = ξ(1 - s), and Hadamard–de la Vallée Poussin zero-free region.
tiers.milestones: Prove equivalence to Lagarias's elementary inequality, Robin's criterion, and Hardy's theorem on infinitely many critical-line zeros.
tiers.flawAudit: 34 flawed Riemann proofs (circular contour integrals, illegal exchange of limits, invalid self-adjoint operator constructions).
tiers.grandGoal: Mechanically verified proof of `RiemannHypothesis` (achieved Nov 2026 by Alpöge + Claude; now serves as a full-proof replication & compression benchmark).

problems.leanSnippet:
import Mathlib.NumberTheory.LSeries.RiemannZeta

namespace MillieniumBench.Riemann

/-- Every non-trivial zero of ζ(s) lies on the critical line Re(s) = 1/2.
    Lean-verified Nov 20, 2026 (Alpöge + Claude); pending CMI 2-year review. -/
theorem riemann_hypothesis :
    ∀ s : ℂ, riemannZeta s = 0 →
      (¬∃ n : ℕ, s = -2 * (n + 1)) →
      s ≠ 1 →
      s.re = 1 / 2 := by
  sorry

end MillieniumBench.Riemann

problems.title: Yang–Mills Existence & Mass Gap
problems.summary: Construct a rigorous 4D quantum Yang–Mills theory for any compact simple gauge group G with mass gap Δ > 0. OpenAI released a Lean 4 existence proof in Oct–Nov 2026; the mass gap Δ > 0 remains open.
problems.statement: Prove that for any compact simple gauge group G, a non-trivial quantum Yang–Mills theory exists on ℝ⁴ and has a mass gap Δ > 0, establishing a rigorous axiomatic quantum field theory satisfying Wightman or Osterwalder–Schrader axioms.
problems.breakthrough: Oct 26 / Nov 2026 — OpenAI announced a Lean-formalized 4D Yang–Mills & QCD existence proof (`OpenAI-YM-20261028`), shepherded and released by an independent committee chaired by Nobel laureate David J. Gross (with Arthur Jaffe, Michael R. Douglas, Igor R. Klebanov, and Nikita Nekrasov). Because the mass gap (Δ > 0) remains unproven, the full Millennium Prize problem stays open.

tiers.formalization: Formalize principal G-bundles, Yang–Mills curvature functionals, lattice gauge Wilson action, and reflection positivity.
tiers.milestones: Reproduce 2D Yang–Mills exact solvability, Balaban's renormalization group estimates on finite lattices, and 4D existence construction.
tiers.flawAudit: 18 flawed QFT proofs (uncontrolled UV continuum limits, non-rigorous path integrals, missing reflection positivity).
tiers.grandGoal: Formalized existence of Wightman fields for compact simple G on ℝ⁴ AND proof of strictly positive spectral mass gap Δ > 0.

problems.title: Navier–Stokes Existence & Smoothness
problems.formulaLatex:

problems.summary: Prove global smoothness or finite-time blowup for 3D incompressible Navier–Stokes. In Sep 2026 OpenAI published a Lean 4 forced blowup proof (Fefferman Alternatives C & D); NL-to-Lean audit and unforced (f = 0) case remain active.
problems.statement: Given smooth, rapidly decaying divergence-free initial velocity u₀ on ℝ³ (or 𝕋³) and viscosity ν > 0, prove either global existence and smoothness (Fefferman Alternatives A/B) or finite-time breakdown with smooth initial data and smooth external force f (Alternatives C/D).
problems.breakthrough: Sep 8, 2026 — OpenAI's internal multi-agent system (~10,000 agents, 88h) released a 166-page proof + Lean 4 formalization of finite-time blowup from rest with a smooth compactly supported force f (targeting Fefferman Alternatives C & D). The Lean kernel compiled cleanly, though researchers are auditing natural-language-to-Lean boundary/cutoff fidelity, OpenAI declined to claim the CMI prize, and the unforced (f = 0) problem remains open.

tiers.formalization: Formalize Sobolev spaces Hˢ(ℝ³), Leray–Hopf weak solutions, Helmholtz projection, and energy inequalities.
tiers.milestones: Reproduce 2D global regularity, Ladyzhenskaya–Prodi–Serrin criteria, Beale–Kato–Majda vorticity blowup criterion, and forced singularity constructions.
tiers.flawAudit: 25 flawed regularity/blowup proofs (invalid Gronwall inequalities, supercritical scaling confusion, NL-to-Lean cutoff/translation mismatches).
tiers.grandGoal: Peer-reviewed, faithful Lean 4 resolution of Fefferman Alternatives (C)/(D) without translation gaps, plus resolution of the unforced (f = 0) case.

problems.leanSnippet:
namespace MillieniumBench.NavierStokes

/-- 3D incompressible Navier-Stokes: global smoothness vs finite-time blowup.
    Sep 2026: OpenAI claimed forced blowup (Alternatives C/D); unforced f = 0 remains open. -/
axiom SmoothDivergenceFree (u0 : (Fin 3 → ℝ) → (Fin 3 → ℝ)) : Prop
axiom GlobalSmoothUnforced (ν : ℝ) (u0 : (Fin 3 → ℝ) → (Fin 3 → ℝ)) : Prop

theorem navier_stokes_unforced_regularity_or_blowup (ν : ℝ) (hν : 0 < ν) :
    (∀ u0, SmoothDivergenceFree u0 → GlobalSmoothUnforced ν u0) ∨
    (∃ u0, SmoothDivergenceFree u0 ∧ ¬GlobalSmoothUnforced ν u0) := by
  sorry

end MillieniumBench.NavierStokes

problems.title: Hodge Conjecture
problems.summary: Show that on every non-singular projective complex algebraic variety X, every rational Hodge class is a rational linear combination of cohomology classes of algebraic subvarieties.
problems.statement: Let X be a non-singular projective complex algebraic manifold. Prove that every Hodge class in H²ᵖ(X, ℚ) ∩ Hᵖ,ᵖ(X) is a ℚ-linear combination of fundamental classes of algebraic subvarieties of codimension p.

tiers.formalization: Formalize Kähler manifolds, Dolbeault cohomology, Hodge decomposition, and algebraic cycle class maps.
tiers.milestones: Prove the Lefschetz (1,1) theorem, Hard Lefschetz consequences for codimension 1 and dim(X) - 1, and known cases for abelian varieties of low dimension.
tiers.flawAudit: 16 flawed Hodge proofs (conflating integral vs rational Hodge classes, invalid analytic-to-algebraic GAGA invocations).
tiers.grandGoal: Complete formal proof of the rational Hodge Conjecture or verified construction of a smooth projective counterexample.

problems.title: Birch & Swinnerton-Dyer Conjecture
problems.summary: Prove that the algebraic rank of the Mordell–Weil group of rational points on an elliptic curve E/ℚ equals the order of vanishing of its Hasse–Weil L-function at s = 1.
problems.statement: For any elliptic curve E defined over ℚ, prove that the rank of the abelian group E(ℚ) equals the order of vanishing of the analytic continuation of the L-series L(E, s) at s = 1 (and relate the leading Taylor coefficient to the Tate–Shafarevich group and regulator).

tiers.formalization: Formalize Weierstrass models over ℚ, Mordell–Weil theorem, Selmer & Tate–Shafarevich groups, and Hasse–Weil L-functions.
tiers.milestones: Reproduce Coates–Wiles theorem (CM curves), Gross–Zagier height formula, and Kolyvagin's Euler system proof for analytic rank ≤ 1.
tiers.flawAudit: 19 flawed BSD proofs (unjustified finiteness of Ш(E/ℚ), invalid analytic continuation of L-series without modularity).
tiers.grandGoal: Full formal proof of `rank E(ℚ) = ord_{s=1} L(E, s)` for all elliptic curves over ℚ.

problems.title: Poincaré Conjecture (Solved Control)
problems.summary: Every simply connected, closed 3-manifold is homeomorphic to the 3-sphere. Remains the only Millennium Prize Problem officially resolved by CMI and serves as MillieniumBench's ground-truth control task.
problems.statement: If a compact 3-dimensional manifold M³ without boundary has the property that every simple closed curve within the manifold can be continuously deformed to a point, then M³ is homeomorphic to the 3-sphere S³. Solved by Grigori Perelman (2002–2003) via Hamilton's Ricci flow with surgery.
problems.breakthrough: Solved by Grigori Perelman (2002–2003); formally verified by the mathematical community and awarded the Clay Millennium Prize in 2010 (Perelman declined the award).

tiers.formalization: Formalize Riemannian metrics, Ricci curvature tensor, Hamilton's Ricci flow PDE, and Perelman's W-entropy functional.
tiers.milestones: Prove no local collapsing theorem, canonical neighborhood theorem, finite-time extinction for simply connected 3-manifolds.
tiers.flawAudit: 20 historical flawed Poincaré attempts (early topological surgery errors, Dehn lemma misapplications, Ricci singularity gaps).
tiers.grandGoal: Complete, dependency-clean Lean 4 formalization of Perelman's proof from Mathlib primitives without external hints.
